questions.prompt: An event \(A\) has \(P(A)=0.32\). Find \(P(A^c)\).
questions.answer: The complement rule gives \[P(A^c)=1-P(A)=1-0.32=0.68.\]

questions.prompt: Events \(A\) and \(B\) are disjoint with \(P(A)=0.25\) and \(P(B)=0.4\). Find \(P(A\cup B)\).
questions.answer: For disjoint events, probabilities add directly: \[P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)=0.25+0.4=0.65.\]

questions.prompt: Events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(P(A)=0.5\), \(P(B)=0.35\), and \(P(A\cap B)=0.1\). Find \(P(A\cup B)\).
questions.answer: Use inclusion-exclusion: \[P(A\cup B)=0.5+0.35-0.1=0.75.\]

questions.prompt: Check whether \(P(A)=1.1\) can be a valid probability.
questions.answer: No. The probability axioms require \(0\le P(A)\le1\) for every event. Since \(1.1>1\), it is invalid.

questions.prompt: A sample space is split into three disjoint events with probabilities \(0.2\), \(0.5\), and \(x\). Find \(x\).
questions.answer: The probabilities of disjoint exhaustive events sum to \(1\). Thus \(0.2+0.5+x=1\), so \(x=0.3\).

questions.prompt: Events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(P(A\cup B)=0.7\), \(P(A)=0.45\), and \(P(B)=0.4\). Find \(P(A\cap B)\).
questions.answer: Rearrange inclusion-exclusion: \[P(A\cap B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cup B)=0.45+0.4-0.7=0.15.\]

questions.prompt: A survey has \(P(A)=0.6\) and \(P(A\cap B)=0.7\). Explain why this is impossible.
questions.answer: The intersection \(A\cap B\) is a subset of \(A\), so \(P(A\cap B)\le P(A)\). The values would require \(0.7\le0.6\), which is impossible.

questions.prompt: If \(P(A^c)=0.18\) and \(P(B)=0.5\), with \(A\) and \(B\) disjoint, can these probabilities be valid?
questions.answer: Since \(P(A)=1-0.18=0.82\), disjointness would require \(P(A\cup B)=0.82+0.5=1.32\). This exceeds \(1\), so the values cannot all be valid.

questions.prompt: Events \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) are disjoint with probabilities \(0.2\), \(0.15\), and \(0.25\). Find the probability that none of them occurs.
questions.answer: The probability that at least one occurs is \(0.2+0.15+0.25=0.6\). Therefore the probability that none occurs is \(1-0.6=0.4\).

questions.prompt: Given \(P(A)=0.7\), \(P(B)=0.6\), find the smallest possible value of \(P(A\cap B)\).
questions.answer: Since \(P(A\cup B)\le1\), inclusion-exclusion gives \(0.7+0.6-P(A\cap B)\le1\). Hence \(P(A\cap B)\ge0.3\), so the smallest possible value is \(0.3\).

questions.prompt: A and B are events with \(P(A)=0.3\), \(P(B)=0.25\), and \(P(A\cap B)=0\). Find \(P(A^c\cap B^c)\).
questions.answer: Since \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), \(P(A\cup B)=0.3+0.25=0.55\). The complement is \(A^c\cap B^c\), so \[P(A^c\cap B^c)=1-0.55=0.45.\]

questions.prompt: A probability model assigns \(P(1)=0.1\), \(P(2)=0.2\), \(P(3)=0.25\), and \(P(4)=0.5\) to four outcomes. Is it valid?
questions.answer: The probabilities must sum to \(1\). Here \(0.1+0.2+0.25+0.5=1.05\), so the model is not valid.

questions.prompt: For events \(A\) and \(B\), \(P(A\setminus B)=0.2\), \(P(A\cap B)=0.15\), and \(P(B\setminus A)=0.25\). Find \(P(A\cup B)\).
questions.answer: The three listed regions are disjoint and together form \(A\cup B\). Therefore \[P(A\cup B)=0.2+0.15+0.25=0.6.\]

questions.prompt: If \(A\subseteq B\), \(P(A)=0.35\), and \(P(B)=0.8\), find \(P(B\cap A^c)\).
questions.answer: Since \(A\subseteq B\), the part of \(B\) outside \(A\) has probability \(P(B)-P(A)=0.8-0.35=0.45\).

questions.prompt: Events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(P(A)=0.62\), \(P(B)=0.48\), and \(P(A\cap B)=0.20\). Find \(P(A^c\cap B^c)\).
questions.answer: First \(P(A\cup B)=0.62+0.48-0.20=0.90\). The complement of \(A\cup B\) is \(A^c\cap B^c\), so the probability is \(1-0.90=0.10\).

questions.prompt: A Venn diagram has regions \(A\) only \(0.18\), \(B\) only \(0.22\), both \(0.31\), and neither \(x\). Find \(x\).
questions.answer: All four disjoint regions must sum to \(1\). Thus \(x=1-(0.18+0.22+0.31)=0.29\).

questions.prompt: Can two events with \(P(A)=0.8\) and \(P(B)=0.75\) be disjoint? Explain.
questions.answer: If they were disjoint, \(P(A\cup B)=0.8+0.75=1.55\), which violates \(P(A\cup B)\le1\). Therefore they cannot be disjoint.

questions.prompt: Events \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) are pairwise disjoint and exhaustive. Given \(P(A)=2P(B)\) and \(P(C)=0.25\), find \(P(A)\) and \(P(B)\).
questions.answer: Since the events are exhaustive, \(P(A)+P(B)+P(C)=1\). Let \(P(B)=x\), so \(P(A)=2x\). Then \(2x+x+0.25=1\), giving \(3x=0.75\) and \(x=0.25\). Thus \(P(B)=0.25\) and \(P(A)=0.50\).

questions.prompt: A proposed model has \(P(A)=0.55\), \(P(B)=0.65\), and \(P(A^c\cap B^c)=0.05\). Find \(P(A\cap B)\) and decide if the model is valid.
questions.answer: Since \(P(A\cup B)=1-P(A^c\cap B^c)=0.95\), inclusion-exclusion gives \(P(A\cap B)=0.55+0.65-0.95=0.25\). This is non-negative and no larger than either \(P(A)\) or \(P(B)\), so these values pass the basic axiom checks.
